sources.title: Revenue NSW: Payroll tax thresholds and rates
sources.fact: Reviewed by Ryan Duguid on 24 September 2026 (page last updated 1 July 2026): 2026-27: tax-free threshold $1,200,000, rate 5.45%. Monthly threshold $92,055 (28 days), $98,630 (30 days), $101,918 (31 days). Threshold apportioned by the NSW share of Australian wages and by days employed.
sources.limitations: Verify the complete page, applicable period and current status at use time.

sources.title: SRO Victoria: Payroll tax current rates
sources.fact: Reviewed by Ryan Duguid on 24 September 2026 (page last updated 10 July 2026): From 1 July 2025: maximum deduction $1,000,000 a year ($83,333 a month); rate 4.85%, 1.2125% for regional Victorian employers. Deduction phases out at 50% for Australian wages between $3 million and $5 million; none above $5 million. Mental health and COVID-19 debt surcharges: combined 1% above $10 million and 2% above $100 million of national payroll, on the Victorian share.
sources.limitations: Verify the complete page, applicable period and current status at use time.

sources.title: Queensland Revenue Office: Payroll tax rates and thresholds
sources.fact: Reviewed by Ryan Duguid on 24 September 2026 (page last updated 17 July 2024 (page footer; modified 3 July 2026)): Rate 4.75% for Australian taxable wages of $6.5 million or less, 4.95% above. Threshold $1.3 million. Regional employers may get a 1% rate discount until 30 June 2030. A mental health levy applies to Queensland wages above its thresholds.
sources.limitations: The mental health levy rates and thresholds were not captured and remain unresolved. Verify the complete page, applicable period and current status at use time.

sources.title: Queensland Revenue Office: Payroll tax deductions
sources.fact: Reviewed by Ryan Duguid on 24 September 2026: Deduction available where annual Australian taxable wages are under $10.4 million; above $1.3 million it reduces by $1 for every $7 of taxable wages, reaching nil at $10.4 million.
sources.limitations: Verify the complete page, applicable period and current status at use time.

sources.title: RevenueWA: Payroll tax calculation
sources.fact: Reviewed by Ryan Duguid on 24 September 2026: Rate 5.5%. Diminishing threshold between annual Australian taxable wages of $1 million and $7.5 million; no deduction at $7.5 million or more. Registration when monthly Australian taxable wages exceed $83,333 (from 1 July 2023).
sources.limitations: Verify the complete page, applicable period and current status at use time.

sources.title: RevenueSA: Payroll tax rates and thresholds
sources.fact: Reviewed by Ryan Duguid on 24 September 2026: From 1 January 2019, by annual Australia-wide taxable payroll: nil up to $1.5 million; a variable rate from 0% to 4.95% above $1.5 million up to $1.7 million; 4.95% above $1.7 million. Registration once Australia-wide wages exceed $1,500,000 a year ($125,000 a month). Maximum deduction $600,000 a year.
sources.limitations: The page's rate table merges columns; the bands above follow its registration threshold and RevenueSA's calculator. Verify the complete page, applicable period and current status at use time.

sources.title: SRO Tasmania: Payroll tax rates and thresholds
sources.fact: Reviewed by Ryan Duguid on 24 September 2026: 2026-27: nil to $1,250,000; 4% from $1,250,001 to $2,000,000; 6.1% above $2,000,000. Monthly threshold is days in month over days in year times the annual amount.
sources.limitations: Verify the complete page, applicable period and current status at use time.

sources.title: ACT Revenue Office: About payroll tax
sources.fact: Reviewed by Ryan Duguid on 24 September 2026: From 1 July 2026 the threshold is $1.75 million a year ($145,833.33 a month), down from $2 million. 2026-27 general rates by Australia-wide wages: 6.75% over $1.75 million to $20 million; 6.85% to $50 million; 7.35% to $100 million; 7.85% to $150 million; 8.75% above $150 million.
sources.limitations: Verify the complete page, applicable period and current status at use time.

sources.title: NT Territory Revenue Office: Payroll tax rates and thresholds
sources.fact: Reviewed by Ryan Duguid on 24 September 2026: July 2026 to June 2027: annual threshold $2,500,000 ($208,333 a month); rate 5.5%, or 6.5% for employers and groups with Australia-wide wages of $100 million or more from 1 July 2026.
